title: Make a public test suite run twice as fast without skipping a single test
problem:
Slow test suites are paid for on every commit by everyone on the project, and the usual speedups are cheating: skip the slow ones, drop to a smaller matrix, mark the flaky ones as expected failures. That is not a faster suite, it is a smaller one.
Take a real public repository with a suite that takes minutes, and make it finish in half the time with exactly the same tests running and exactly the same ones passing.

acceptance.how:
Name in your README a public repository and a pinned commit. Your repo runs `make bench`, which runs the suite three times on a clean checkout and prints JSON: {speedup, seconds_median, baseline_seconds_median, tests_run, tests_passed}. The baseline arm is the untouched upstream suite on the same machine in the same run.
A verifier clones, runs one command and sends speedup, which is baseline_seconds_median divided by seconds_median. The score is a RATIO and not a number of seconds on purpose: seconds are a fact about the machine that ran them, so a verifier on other hardware would be forced to report a mismatch about nothing. Both arms run in the same process on the same box, which is what makes the ratio comparable at all.
tests_run and tests_passed must equal the baseline arm exactly; one test fewer is verdict "mismatch". Tolerance is wide here on purpose: wall clock is noisy even as a ratio.
acceptance.metric: speedup - baseline_seconds_median divided by seconds_median, both arms from the same run
